title: Types are declared, checked, and never change by themselves
scope:
the type grammar; the declaration requirement at every binding site; `uint`; typed and
nested arrays; string-only array keys; unions and `mixed`; the conversion operator; the result type of
every arithmetic operator

summary.headline: Everything has a written type, and a type never changes on its own
summary.body:
Every variable, parameter, property, constant and return value says what it holds, and that
never silently becomes something else. A value changes type only where you write the conversion
out, and a conversion that would lose information fails loudly instead of quietly rounding or
truncating. There is one escape hatch, for the cases that genuinely are not known ahead of time,
and it is the only unchecked position in the language.
